questions.q: What does it mean for a pipeline step to be idempotent?
options: It runs faster each time it's executed
Running it twice with the same input produces the same result as running it once
It never raises exceptions
It only works with SQLite databases
questions.explain: Idempotency means reruns don't make the target worse - they land in the same end state.

questions.q: What problem does load_append_only() have if the pipeline is run twice?
options: It deletes all existing rows
It creates duplicate rows, since if_exists="append" has no idea the data was already loaded
It raises an error on the second run
It automatically merges duplicate rows
questions.explain: Appending blindly on every run means a rerun doubles up every row that was already loaded.

questions.q: What does order_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY accomplish in load_upsert()'s table definition?
options: It makes order_id the table's unique key, which INSERT OR REPLACE can target
It converts order_id into a text column
It deletes the column if it's ever duplicated
It has no effect on INSERT OR REPLACE
questions.explain: INSERT OR REPLACE relies on the primary key to decide whether to insert a new row or replace an existing one.

questions.q: What does SQLite's INSERT OR REPLACE do when a row with a matching primary key already exists?
options: It raises an error and stops
It skips that row silently
It replaces the existing row in place instead of creating a duplicate
It appends a duplicate row anyway
questions.explain: This is SQLite's upsert behavior - replace on key match, insert otherwise.

questions.q: Why does idempotency simplify recovering from a failed pipeline run?
options: Because you never need to fix the underlying cause of the failure
Because the whole pipeline can simply be rerun from the top without creating duplicates, instead of figuring out exactly which rows made it in
Because idempotent steps never fail in the first place
Because it removes the need for a try/except block entirely
questions.explain: An idempotent load means a full rerun safely re-upserts everything, with no duplicate-row cleanup needed.
